prompt:
Write two bash functions.
1. rev_words: takes one string argument and prints its words in reverse order separated by single spaces (runs of spaces are collapsed; leading and trailing spaces are ignored). An empty or blank argument prints an empty line.
2. is_palindrome: takes one string argument and returns exit status 0 if it is a palindrome when ignoring case and every non-alphanumeric character, 1 otherwise. An empty string is a palindrome. It prints nothing.
Use only bash builtins and coreutils. Reply with a single ```bash code block containing only the two functions, no explanations.
tests:
t(){ if [ "$2" == "$3" ]; then echo "PASS $1"; else echo "FAIL $1"; fi; }
t rw1 "c b a" "$(rev_words 'a b  c')"
t rw2 "" "$(rev_words '')"
t rw3 "world hello" "$(rev_words '  hello   world ')"
t rw4 "one" "$(rev_words 'one')"
p(){ if is_palindrome "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; then r=0; else r=1; fi; if [ "$r" == "$3" ]; then echo "PASS $1"; else echo "FAIL $1"; fi; }
p pa1 "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" 0
p pa2 "racecar" 0
p pa3 "hello" 1
p pa4 "" 0
p pa5 "No 'x' in Nixon" 0
p pa6 "ab" 1
